calls.reason: The released data confirm all five expert threshold differences were positive, and 1/32 is correct for independent fair signs. But the same participants did all five tasks, so the independence the significance claim needs is unestablished.

OpenAI's narrative reports a 0.88-point expert accuracy uplift out of 10, and Marcus quoted it accurately. OpenAI's released summary data actually average about 0.97, which supports a lift at least that large.

The packet found no study comparing open-weight and guarded commercial models, only a study of two Llama variants and a review calling for evaluations. That is suggestive but thin, so it does not clearly settle what was known at the time.

OpenAI's report and the Bloomberg, Verge, Gizmodo and Maginative articles were checked in full. None highlights the fourfold formulation result or discusses the Esvelt-lab study in substance; OpenAI only cites it.
OpenAI's participant-level data show 25 experts in each arm. Four LLM-assisted experts and one internet-only expert reached the 8/10 formulation threshold, which is exactly the fourfold sample ratio.

OpenAI's own report calls the differences not statistically significant and acknowledges limited statistical power. It leaves practical importance open rather than showing an important positive effect is absent.
